nodes.name: NaₓWO₃ Hydrothermal + Multi-temperature Annealing
nodes.procedure: 2 mmol sodium tungstate dihydrate (Na₂WO₄·2H₂O) and 0.5 mmol ammonium fluoride (NH₄F) were dissolved in a mixed solution of 40 mL deionized water and 20 mL absolute alcohol under vigorous stirring. Then, the resultant mixed solution together with a piece of pretreated NF (2×4 cm²) immersed in it was transferred into a 100 mL Teflon-lined autoclave. Subsequently, the autoclave was heated to 150°C and kept for 10 h in an oven. After cooled down to room temperature, the obtained NF covered with the precursor of W and Na was washed with deionized water and dried in vacuum under 60°C. Finally, the obtained precursor was annealed in a tube furnace at 350°C, 500°C and 650°C for 2 h under a mixed H₂/Ar (5 vol% H₂) atmosphere to obtain different NaₓWO₃ samples, which were denoted as NaₓWO₃-350, NaₓWO₃-500 and NaₓWO₃-650, respectively.

nodes.name: MₓWO₃ Solvothermal (M=K,Rb,Cs)
nodes.procedure: 0.8 mmol tungsten hexachloride (WCl₆) and 1 mmol MCl (M = K, Rb and Cs) were dissolved in 50 mL absolute alcohol under vigorous stirring. Then, the resultant mixed solution together with a piece of pretreated NF (2×4 cm²) immersed in it was transferred into a 100 mL Teflon-lined autoclave. Subsequently, the autoclave was heated to 200°C and kept for 12 h in an oven. After cooled down to room temperature, NF covered with the KₓWO₃, RbₓWO₃ and CsₓWO₃ were obtained, washed with deionized water and dried in vacuum under 60°C.

nodes.name: WO₃ Thermal Decomposition
nodes.procedure: 2 mmol Na₂WO₄·2H₂O was dissolved in 50 mL deionized water and then 10 mL concentrated nitric acid was slowly added and kept stirring for 12 h under room temperature. Then, a yellow precipitate was firstly obtained after remove the above solution by filtration, and then washed with deionized water for several times and vacuum-dried at 60°C. Finally, the collected yellow precursor was annealed in a tube furnace at 500°C for 2 h under the mixed H₂/Ar atmosphere to obtain the WO₃ product.

nodes.characterization_summary: Na_xWO3-500 exhibits porous octahedron morphology with preserved structure after annealing at 500°C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For Na_xWO3-500, the SEM images (Fig. 2c and Figure S5c) show that the octahedron morphology is still preserved after annealed under 500°C, and interestingly, the surface of the monolith becomes obviously porous...

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms porous structure of Na_xWO3 with lattice fringe of 0.269 nm corresponding to (110) planes of cubic Na_xWO3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 2e presents the TEM image of Na_xWO3, in which the porous structure can be clearly observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows crystal lattice fringe with interplanar spacing of 0.269 nm corresponding to (110) planes of cubic Na_xWO3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the HRTEM image presented in Fig. 2f, the crystal lattice fringe with an interplanar spacing of 0.269 nm, corresponding to the (110) planes of cubic Na_xWO3, is observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED patterns exhibit clear diffraction rings indexing to (100), (110), (210), and (211) planes of cubic Na_xWO3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Meanwhile, as shown in Fig. 2g, the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) patterns exhibit clear diffraction rings indexing to the (100), (110), (210), and (211) planes of a cubic Na_xWO3.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX shows uniform distribution of W, O, Na elements; Na:W ratio 12.31:18.76 at% corresponding to x≈0.66.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the EDX spectrum (Figure S8), Na and W elements in the Na_xWO3 is determined to be 12.31 and 18.76 at% respectively, corresponding to x≈0.66.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms cubic Na_{0.69}WO3 structure (PDF #75-0236) with diffraction peaks at 23.16°, 32.99°, 40.69° etc.

Na 1s peak at 1071.1 eV confirms Na+; W 4f shows W6+ (35.3/37.4 eV) and W5+ (34.5/36.4 eV) with stronger W5+ intensity than precursor; O 1s shows lattice oxygen at 530.5 eV and surface oxygen at 532.4 eV (no Ov peak unlike WO3).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution Na 1 s spectrum of Na_xWO3 displays a peak centered at 1071.1 eV... For Na2O·WO3·H2O and Na_xWO3, the W 4 f spectra can be deconvoluted into two components, which are assigned to W6+ (35.3/37.4 eV) and W5+ (34.5/36.4 eV). Especially, the intensity of W5+ in Na_xWO3 is obviously stronger than in Na2O·WO3·H2O... As demonstrated in Fig. 3d, the O 1 s spectra of Na2O·WO3·H2O and Na_xWO3 mainly exhibit two components, corresponding to lattice oxygen (M-O, 530.5 eV) and surface oxygen (Os, 532.4 eV), yet as a contrast, an additional signal associated with the oxygen vacancies (Ov, 531.3 eV) in the WO3 sample can be obviously observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: No EPR signal at g=2.003 for Na_xWO3, confirming absence of oxygen vacancies unlike WO3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As seen Fig. 3e, WO3 displays a typical EPR signal at g = 2.003, confirming oxygen vacancies existing in it, while Na2O·WO3·H2O and Na_xWO3 show no obvious EPR signals, indicating the absence of electron trapping by oxygen vacancies.

nodes.characterization_summary: Apparent conductivity of Na_xWO3 is 3 times higher than WO3 and 309 times higher than precursor.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As seen in Fig. 3f, the apparent conductivity of Na_xWO3 is 3 and 309 times higher than that of WO3 and Na2O·WO3·H2O, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: W L3-edge XANES shifts to lower energy; EXAFS shows enhanced W-O coordination; coordination number 5.9, W-O bond 1.91 Å vs WO3 (5.4, 1.77 Å).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The coordination number of W atoms in WO3 is determined to be 5.4, and the average length of W-O bonds is 1.77 Å. In contrast, the coordination number of W in Na_xWO3 is 5.9 and the average length of W-O bonds is 1.91 Å.

nodes.characterization_summary: W L3-edge XANES absorption edge shifts to lower binding energy vs WO3; white-line peak between W foil and WO3 indicates moderate W oxidation state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 3g presents the X-ray absorption near-edge spectroscopy (XANES) at the W L3-edge of Na_xWO3 and the control samples. Compared to WO3, the absorption edge of W in Na_xWO3 shifts to a lower binding energy... Besides, the white-line peak of Na_xWO3 locates between those of W foil and WO3, indicating the moderate oxidation of W due to different local atomic arrangements.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fourier transform EXAFS shows enhanced W-O peak intensity vs WO3 (1.0-2.0 Å); coordination number 5.9 and W-O bond length 1.91 Å vs WO3 (5.4, 1.77 Å); wavelet transform confirms W-O coordination at 6.0-7.0 Å⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 3h the Fourier transform extended XAFS (EXAFS) of Na_xWO3 and the control samples, the peaks locating at 1.0-2.0 Å for WO3 and Na_xWO3 are ascribed to W-O coordination... It should be noted that, the W-O peak intensity in Na_xWO3 is obviously higher than that in WO3... Furthermore, the quantitative structural configurations... coordination number of W in Na_xWO3 is 5.9 and the average length of W-O bonds is 1.91 Å.
